(NASDAQ:IRON), a clinical stage biopharmaceutical company focused on the discovery, development, and commercialization of novel treatments for patients suffering from serious hematologic diseases, today announced topline results from the APOLLO Phase 3 trial of bitopertin in erythropoietic protoporphyria (EPP), including X-linked protoporphyria (XLP).

Summary of topline results: • Bitopertin achieved statistical significance on both co-primary endpoints vs. placebo: • Reduction in whole-blood metal-free PPIX from baseline (-41.4% vs. placebo, p<0.0001) • Increase in average monthly total time in light without pain during month 6 (+12.2 hours vs. placebo, p=0.0010) • Bitopertin achieved statistical significance on all secondary endpoints vs. placebo, including: • Reduction in incidence rate of phototoxic reactions over the 6-month treatment period vs. placebo (p<0.0001) • Increase in cumulative total time in light without pain over the 6-month treatment period vs. placebo (p<0.0001) • Increase in change from baseline in average daily sunlight exposure time to prodrome vs. placebo (p=0.0077, adults only) • Bitopertin demonstrated additional quality of life benefits vs. placebo, including improved Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC) score (p<0.0001) and Patient Global Impression of Severity (PGIS) score (p<0.0001) • Bitopertin was generally well-tolerated.
Management will host a corporate webcast this morning, Monday, October 19 at 8:00am EST to discuss the APOLLO topline results and next steps.
